title: Composition–property correlations of SiO 2  content in CO 2 -based PPC/ionic-liquid composite zinc electrolytes
content: The performance of multicomponent polymer electrolytes for Zn batteries is governed collectively by the local ionic environment, bulk ion transport, Zn2+-associated steady-state response, and electrode/electrolyte interfaces. Here, laboratory-synthesized CO2-based poly(propylene carbonate) (PPC) was used as a film-forming matrix, together with PYR13TFSI, Zn(TFSI)2, and varying contents of SiO2, to construct PPC/PYR13TFSI/Zn(TFSI)2/SiO2 solid-state composite polymer electrolytes. Systematic composition–property correlations were established between SiO2 content and multiscale properties in a fixed PPC/PYR13TFSI/Zn(TFSI)2 ternary matrix. Because PPC incorporates CO2 as a comonomer-derived carbon source, this material platform provides a CO2-valorization-oriented electrolyte design. XRD showed that all samples retained predominantly amorphous polymer matrices, whereas FTIR and peak-fitted O 1s/XPS data revealed composition-dependent changes in the local chemical environments of PPC oxygen-containing groups, TFSI− anions, and Zn-salt species after SiO2 incorporation. PIZS-3 (3 wt% SiO2) delivered the lowest bulk resistance, a room-temperature ionic conductivity of approximately 6.0 × 10−4 S cm−1, and the highest apparent Zn2+ transference number (0.556). Under stepwise current-density tests at 0.5–5.0 mA cm−2 with 1 mAh cm−2 per half-cycle, both Zn|PIZ|Zn and Zn|PIZS-3|Zn cells exhibited stable reversible voltage profiles. The Zn|PIZS-3|Zn symmetric cell operated stably for more than 1200 h at 1 mA cm−2 and 1 mAh cm−2 per half-cycle (1 h per half-cycle), evidencing robust Zn–metal interfacial behavior. The V2O5|PIZS-3|Zn full cell also exhibited excellent cycling stability, whereas PIZS-7 delivered the highest rate capacity within the tested SiO2 range of 0–7 wt%. These results identify ca. 3 wt% SiO2 as an optimal composition window for balancing bulk transport and Zn–metal interfacial response, while higher SiO2 contents favor rate capability in full cells.
